---
title: "The AI economy"
---

What AI is and is not doing to the U.S. economy right now.

## Investment

<!-- Draft: rewrite before publishing. -->
Much of the equipment behind the AI buildout is imported, so its boost to U.S. output is smaller than the investment spending suggests.

{{< include charts/ai-investment-gdp/output/ai-investment-gdp-lead.md >}}

## Adoption

<!-- Draft: rewrite before publishing. -->
Surveys disagree about how widely AI is used. Part of the gap is who they count, firms or workers, and part is what they ask.

{{< include charts/ai-adoption/output/ai-adoption-lead.md >}}

```{=html}
<picture>
  <source media="(max-width: 600px)" srcset="charts/ai-adoption/output/ai-adoption-narrow.png">
  <img src="charts/ai-adoption/output/ai-adoption.png" class="chart" alt="Line chart of the share of U.S. firms, workers, and jobs using AI from 2023 to 2026. About a quarter of firms used AI in September 2026 after Census widened its question in November 2025, which lifted the firm share from 10 to 17 percent. About 45 percent of workers used generative AI for their job in May 2026, and one survey put 78 percent of jobs at firms using AI in November 2025.">
</picture>
```

{{< include charts/ai-adoption/output/ai-adoption-notes.md >}}

## Productivity

<!-- Draft: rewrite before publishing. -->
Productivity growth has been strong, but most of it comes from businesses working their existing staff and equipment harder and from investment in computers and software, not from efficiency gains.

{{< include charts/productivity-decomposition/output/productivity-decomposition-lead.md >}}

```{=html}
<picture>
  <source media="(max-width: 600px)" srcset="charts/productivity-decomposition/output/productivity-decomposition-narrow.png">
  <img src="charts/productivity-decomposition/output/productivity-decomposition.png" class="chart" alt="Stacked bar chart of contributions to U.S. business sector labor productivity growth from 2022 to 2026. Since 2025, most growth comes from higher utilization and from computer and software capital, while total factor productivity contributes little and turns negative in the latest quarter.">
</picture>
```
